reason: Steel is a plausible frame for the shared growing beds.
expectation: The steel will form or support the bed structure on the floor.

alternatives.reason: The liner might need to be fitted to a steel frame before installation.

effect: The steel formed raised frames with outlets positioned above the future reservoir.
reaction: The different bed depths make the crops' needs tangible.
reason: The food-safe sheet should line the newly built frames to hold the growing beds.
expectation: The sheet will line the bed frames while accommodating their outlets.

alternatives.reason: The reservoir also belongs beneath the bed outlets.

effect: The frames are lined, but their drain stubs still need a hose to reach the reservoir.
reaction: The distinction between the load-bearing frames and the liner is clear.
reason: The clean service hose should connect the open drains to the reservoir.
expectation: The hose will connect the bed drains, or prepare them for connection to the reservoir.

alternatives.reason: The reservoir must also be positioned beneath the beds.

effect: The drains now fall toward the reservoir, and the next goal is to complete the return-water system.
reaction: The gravity-fed drainage is a sensible detail.
reason: The reservoir and pump belong beneath the connected drains to collect and recirculate water.
expectation: The reservoir and pump will connect to the beds' drainage system.

effect: The failed direct pairing automatically fitted the hose to the reservoir, creating an aerating return reservoir ready to connect to the drained beds.
reaction: The compatibility feedback was useful, though I had expected the reservoir to attach directly.
reason: The prepared reservoir and drained beds appear ready to be joined into the return-water system.
expectation: The bed drains will connect to the reservoir, completing the aerated return system.

effect: The drains and reservoir are connected, completing the shared growing-bed system and the chapter.
reaction: The separate depth and flow adjustments make the shared system feel practical.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the drains to the aerating reservoir was most worthwhile: it brought the separate pieces together while explaining how the crops can share water but retain different root-zone settings.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate drain-hose and reservoir-hose steps were a little confusing, particularly because the first hose result already described water falling toward the reservoir.

surprise.text: The attempted direct reservoir connection instead prompted an automatic hose fitting; the reservoir then still needed to be joined to the bed drains.

arbitrary.text: The need to fit a service hose separately to the reservoir was not obvious from the preceding drain description, though the resulting aeration had a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would continue: the physical explanations made the construction satisfying, and I would be curious to see the empty beds put to use.
